data.summary: Frequency tables and diagrams organise data. A cumulative frequency curve gives median and quartiles by reading across and down.
key_concepts: Grouped frequency tables use class intervals; read inequality signs carefully when tallying
A cumulative frequency curve plots running total against the upper class boundary
Median at n/2; lower quartile at n/4; upper quartile at 3n/4 on the vertical axis

worked_examples.question: A cumulative frequency curve covers 200 students. Explain how to find the median and how many scored more than 70.
steps: For the median, read across from 100 on the CF axis to the curve, then down to the marks axis
For scores above 70, read up from 70 to find how many scored 70 or less
worked_examples.answer: Median at CF = 100; number above 70 = 200 - CF reading at 70

common_mistakes.mistake: Reading the median halfway along the marks axis.
common_mistakes.fix: Read at half the total frequency on the vertical (CF) axis.

common_mistakes.mistake: Plotting cumulative frequency against the class midpoint.
common_mistakes.fix: Plot against the upper class boundary.

common_mistakes.mistake: Misreading class inequalities when building a frequency table.
common_mistakes.fix: Check whether the interval uses < or <= before tallying.

exam_tips: Draw reading lines onto the graph to show your method.
Check the curve finishes at the total frequency.
